misconceptions.description: Assuming porous structures are automatically weak
misconceptions.trigger: learner equates empty space with structural failure
misconceptions.feedback: Cellular solids can remain mechanically efficient because geometry channels loads through walls, ribs, and repeating cells rather than relying only on bulk mass.

misconceptions.description: Assuming weight reduction has no mechanical cost
misconceptions.trigger: learner removes material without discussing stiffness, buckling, or fatigue limits
misconceptions.feedback: Biomimetic lightweighting is a trade study. Removing material lowers mass, but it can also reduce stiffness, durability, or impact tolerance if the geometry is not tuned carefully.

misconceptions.description: Treating biomimicry as literal copying of natural form
misconceptions.trigger: learner proposes copying honeycomb visually without abstracting the structural principle
misconceptions.feedback: Engineering biomimicry usually abstracts a principle such as load distribution or material efficiency rather than copying nature at full scale without modification.
